DeltaChunksResponse.description:
Response of `PUT /api/files/delta/chunks` — the server-computed identity
of every received frame, in wire order. Clients compare against their
own hashes to detect corruption before committing.

DeltaCommitRequest.description:
Request body of `POST /api/files/delta/commit`.

Exactly one of (`name` + `folder_id`) or `file_id` selects the mode:
create a new file, or replace an existing file's content.

chunks.description: Full chunk sequence, in file order (per occurrence).

file_hash.description: BLAKE3 of the complete file (verified server-side, never trusted).

file_id.description: Update mode: file whose content is replaced (caller needs Write).

folder_id.description: Create mode: target folder (caller needs Create permission).

DeltaDownloadRequest.description:
Request body of `POST /api/files/delta/download` — distinct chunk
hashes to fetch, served back as `[u32 BE length][bytes]` frames in
request order (the same wire format the upload direction uses).

DeltaManifestResponse.description:
Response of `GET /api/files/{id}/manifest` — the recipe to rebuild the
file from chunks. Immutable for a given `file_hash`, so clients cache
it keyed by hash (the endpoint also serves it with `ETag: file_hash`).

chunks.description: Full chunk sequence, in file order (per occurrence).

file_hash.description: BLAKE3 of the whole file (verify the local reassembly against it).

chunks.description: The file's chunks, in order (duplicates allowed — repeated content).

missing.description: Distinct chunk hashes the caller must upload (first-occurrence order).

DeltaNotAvailableResponse.description:
404 body of `POST /api/files/delta/download` when some requested chunks
are not reachable through the caller's files (or don't exist — the two
are deliberately indistinguishable).

DeltaStillMissingResponse.description:
409 body of `POST /api/files/delta/commit` when chunks vanished between
negotiate and commit (GC race) or were never claimable: the client
uploads exactly these hashes and retries the same commit.

DpopBindDto.description: Post-redirect DPoP bind DTO — only field is the JWK thumbprint.

dpop_jkt.description:
Base64url SHA-256 of the canonical public-key JWK (RFC 7638) —
exactly 43 characters, `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`.

DriveDto.description:
One row in `GET /api/drives` — a drive the caller can read.

`default_for_user` is `Some(<caller_id>)` for the caller's default
Personal drive and `None` otherwise. The picker UI uses this to put
the default at the top of the list and mark it as "your home".

oneOf.description:
Highest role the **calling** user holds on this drive (direct OR
group-mediated). Populated by `GET /api/drives` and the drive
grants in `/api/grants/incoming/resources`. Omitted (`None`) in
contexts where the caller isn't naturally a member — e.g. the
outgoing-grants listing where the caller is the granter and may
not have a current role on the drive themselves.

**UI gating**:
- `Some(Owner)` → mutation controls (add/edit/remove members, change policies, delete drive)
- `Some(Editor/Contributor/Commenter)` → mutate drive contents, no membership UI
- `Some(Viewer)` → read-only
- `None` → show neither member list nor mutation controls

See `project_caller_role_on_file_folder_dto` memory for the
pattern extension to FileDto / FolderDto (deferred, perf-sensitive).

name.description:
Display name. Sourced from `storage.folders.name` of the row
pointed at by `root_folder_id` (drives have no `name` column —
see docs/plan/drive.md §3). The wire shape is unchanged from
the client's perspective.

policies.description:
Capability-flag bag — clients render UI affordances based on
known keys (`forbid_public_links`, `include_in_photo_index`,
`forbid_music_index`, …). Unknown keys preserved verbatim.

quota_bytes.description:
Storage cap in bytes. `None` means "no quota" (admin override /
future system drives). Mutation is OxiCloud-admin only — drive
owners cannot self-grant capacity.

root_folder_id.description:
The drive's mount-point folder. Folder API calls
(`POST /api/folders { parent_id: <root_folder_id> }`,
`PATCH /api/folders/<root_folder_id>` to rename) use this id —
no polymorphic "create at drive root" surface needed.

used_bytes.description:
Running total of bytes consumed. Maintained incrementally in D4;
on D0 this reflects the backfilled baseline.

EffectiveLinkDto.description:
A public link on an ancestor folder (or the drive) that also reaches
the requested folder.

Carries the share's own metadata — a token grant alone would give a
client nothing to show but an opaque id.

**Not [`ShareDto`](crate::application::dtos::share_dto::ShareDto),
deliberately.** That type carries `token` and `url` — the live
secret — which is right when handing someone a link they own, and
wrong here. The caller holds `Share` on a DESCENDANT; the ancestor's
link may publish the whole ancestor tree, so "something above you is
published, here is where" is the honest payload and a working URL is
an escalation they never visited that folder to earn. Both fields
are non-`Option` there, so reuse would mean `""` — a value a client
could build a broken link from.

`expires_at` is the GRANT's, not the share row's. The two can
diverge, and the grant is what actually gates access.

grant_id.description: `storage.role_grants.id` of the token grant. Stable list key.

has_password.description: Whether opening the link requires a password.

name.description: Operator-given link name. `None` when the creator never set one.

resource.description:
Where the link lives — the folder or drive carrying the grant.
Clients resolve a folder's display name from `ancestors`.

share_id.description:
The share this link belongs to (`storage.shares.id`, which is the
token grant's subject).

FaceBoxDto.description: One face box within a photo (for tagging overlays in the lightbox).

FavoriteItemDto.description:
DTO for favorites item, enriched with item metadata via SQL JOIN
so the frontend does not need N+1 requests to resolve names/sizes.

created_at.description: When the item was added to favorites

icon_class.description: FontAwesome icon CSS class (e.g. "fas fa-file-image", "fas fa-folder")

icon_special_class.description: Extra CSS class for icon styling (e.g. "image-icon", "folder-icon")

id.description: Unique identifier for the favorite entry

item_id.description: ID of the favorited item (file or folder)

item_name.description: Display name of the file or folder

item_path.description:
Full human-readable path (e.g. "Documents/Work" for a folder,
"Documents/Work/report.pdf" for a file)

item_size.description: Size in bytes (files only; folders → None)

modified_at.description: Last modification timestamp of the item

parent_id.description: Parent folder ID (folder_id for files, parent_id for folders)

size_formatted.description: Formatted file size (e.g. "3.27 MB"); "--" for folders

user_id.description: User ID who owns this favorite

favorited_at.description: When the resource was added to the user's favorites.

resource.description: Full resource details — shape determined by `resource_type`.

FeaturesDto.description:
Feature-flag block within [`ServerConfigDto`]. One boolean per
optional subsystem. Adding a new feature: append a field with a
default that matches the server-side default; NEVER remove a field
(client code may depend on the absence of a `false` value to mean
"unknown").

faces.description:
Face detection + identity clustering ("People"). Biometric —
OFF by default. See `FeaturesConfig::enable_faces`.

markdown_collab.description:
Collaborative `.md` editing over the message-bus WebSocket
(Yjs CRDT). When `false`, the FE hides the "New markdown"
menu entry and falls back to the plain `.md` viewer when
opening one. See `FeaturesConfig::enable_markdown_collab`.

message_bus.description:
Message bus over WebSocket. When `false`, `/api/rt/ws` and
`/api/rt/ticket` are not registered — clients skip WS setup
entirely. See `FeaturesConfig::enable_message_bus`.

sharing.description:
File sharing (public share links + user-to-user grants). See
`FeaturesConfig::enable_file_sharing`.

trash.description:
Recycle bin / soft-delete flow. When `false`, deletes are
permanent — no `/api/trash` endpoint. See
`FeaturesConfig::enable_trash`.

video_thumbnails.description:
Server-side video-thumbnail generation via ffmpeg. See
`FeaturesConfig::enable_video_thumbnails`.

content_hash.description:
Raw BLAKE3 content hash. Populated from `File::content_hash()`.
Exposed in REST JSON so API consumers can use it for
content-addressable URLs, dedup verification, and integrity
audits. Distinct from `etag` (which is an HTTP-only cache
token whose formula may grow to include `modified_at` etc.).

created_by.description:
§14 provenance: user that originally created this file.
`None` when the referenced user has been deleted (FK is
`ON DELETE SET NULL`) or for stub/legacy files.

etag.description:
Opaque HTTP ETag. Populated from `File::etag()`. Used by
WebDAV/NextCloud handlers when emitting `ETag` headers and
also exposed in REST JSON so frontends can pass it back
through `If-Match` / `If-None-Match` on download / mutation
endpoints without a separate HEAD round-trip.

icon_special_class.description: Extra CSS class for icon styling (e.g. "image-icon", "" when default)

is_favorite.description:
Caller-scoped: `true` when the requesting user has favorited
this file. **Wire contract: always present**, never null and
never absent — the SPA reads it as a required `boolean` with no
nullish branch. Every emission path (listing endpoints inline
via a per-row `EXISTS` in the listing SQL; single-item endpoints
via the shared `caller_flags` helper on the favorites port) is
responsible for populating this before the DTO reaches the
wire. WebDAV/CalDAV/CardDAV DTOs default to `false` — the XML
property serializer drops the field entirely, so a stale
default is never observable on those surfaces.

is_shared.description:
Resource-scoped: `true` when the file has ANY explicit
role-grant on it (link share via `subject_type = 'token'`,
user/group grant, any role). "Someone was given access to
this beyond drive membership." Same wire contract as
`is_favorite` — always present.

mime_type.description:
MIME type — `Arc<str>` because MIME values repeat across files
and DTOs are cloned on every request (clone is O(1) atomic increment).

sort_date.description:
Sort date for Photos timeline — COALESCE(EXIF captured_at, created_at).
Only populated by the /api/photos endpoint.

updated_by.description:
§14 provenance: user that performed the most recent mutation
that bumped `updated_at`. Authorship signal — distinct from
`owner_id`. `None` when the referenced user is deleted or for
stub/legacy files.

FolderAncestorDto.description:
Single crumb in the walk from the drive root (or share-boundary) down
to the leaf. Present only for ancestors the caller has Read on; the
walk stops at the first inaccessible parent.

drive_id.description:
Drive the folder belongs to. Always populated (every folder has
a drive_id in the D0+ schema). Lets clients derive the current
drive from `ancestors.at(-1).drive_id` without a second
`GET /api/folders/{id}` round-trip — the ancestors response is
the authoritative "everything I need for the folder-context
header" call. See 2026-07-26 UX pass on /files load traffic.

parent_id.description:
`None` on the drive-root folder. On boundary crumbs it's the id
of the (invisible-to-caller) parent — clients don't render it
but the field is preserved for debugging.

FolderAncestorsDto.description:
Response envelope for `GET /api/folders/{id}/ancestors`.

`ancestors` is root-first (drive root or share boundary as element
0), leaf-last. Length ≥ 1 (the leaf itself is always included).
`access_source` describes the boundary at element 0.

effective_grants.description:
Every grant that reaches the leaf: its own, each visible
ancestor's, and the drive's. Answers "who can get at this
folder, and through what?" — a question the per-resource grant
listing cannot, because it only ever reports direct rows.

**Present only for `?include_grants=true`.** Omitted otherwise
because the breadcrumb calls this endpoint on every folder
navigation and must not start paying for a grants query it never
reads.

No separate "source" field: each [`GrantDto`] already names the
resource it sits on, so a client tells direct from inherited by
comparing `resource.id` against the leaf, and resolves an
inherited grant's display name from `ancestors` — which it
already has in the same response.

Safe by construction: the ancestor walk drops folders the caller
cannot Read (see `get_ancestors_with_perms`), and this only
collects grants for ancestors that survived. A caller can never
learn of a folder — or of who holds access to one — that they
could not already see.

effective_links.description:
Public links that reach the leaf, from the same walk.

Split out of `effective_grants` rather than mixed in: a link is
not a subject. It has no name to resolve, no role to change and
nobody to notify, and clients render it in a different place
entirely. Keeping both in one list made every consumer
re-partition by `subject.type` before it could draw anything.

Same presence rule as `effective_grants` — only for
`?include_grants=true`.

created_by.description:
§14 provenance: user that originally created this folder.
`None` when the referenced user has been deleted (FK is
`ON DELETE SET NULL`) or for stub/legacy folders.

drive_id.description:
Drive that owns this folder. The scope axis for path-based
lookups across REST / WebDAV / NextCloud / CalDAV / CardDAV.
Post-D0 `storage.folders.drive_id` is `NOT NULL`; stub /
DTO-reconstructed folders carry `Uuid::nil()`.

etag.description:
Opaque ETag for HTTP responses. Populated from `Folder::etag()`
at conversion time so every WebDAV / NextCloud handler emits
the same value, and exposed in REST JSON so the frontend can
pass it back through `If-Match` on rename / move endpoints
without a separate HEAD round-trip.

icon_special_class.description: Extra CSS class for icon styling (always "folder-icon")

is_favorite.description:
Caller-scoped: `true` when the requesting user has favorited
this folder. See `FileDto::is_favorite` for the full wire
contract note (always present, never null; enrichment path
covers listing rows via inline `EXISTS` and single-item
endpoints via the `caller_flags` helper).

is_root.description: Whether this is a root folder

is_shared.description:
Resource-scoped: `true` when the folder has ANY explicit
role-grant on it. Same wire contract as `is_favorite`.

updated_by.description:
§14 provenance: user that performed the most recent mutation
that bumped `updated_at`. Authorship signal — distinct from
`owner_id`. `None` when the referenced user is deleted or for
stub/legacy folders.

FolderListingDto.description:
Combined DTO that returns both sub-folders and files for a given folder
in a single response, eliminating the double-fetch on every navigation.

favorite_ids.description:
Ids (folders + files in this listing) the caller has favorited. Lets the
client render star badges without a separate per-navigation favorites
fetch. Sorted for a stable response / ETag.

shared_ids.description:
Ids in this listing the caller has an outgoing share/grant on (incl.
public links). Sorted for a stable response / ETag.

FolderResourceItemDto.description:
One item in a `/resources` page — a file or folder with a `resource_type` tag.
Re-uses [`ResourceContentDto`] so the shape is identical to `SharedWithMeItemDto.resource`.

resource.description: Full resource details. Shape is determined by `resource_type`.

FullUserDto.description:
Full user record — public identity + all fields BOTH an admin
(viewing another user) AND the subject themselves may see. Returned
as `Vec<FullUserDto>` by `/api/admin/users`; embedded in
[`SelfUserDto`] for `/api/auth/me`.

This is the DTO closest to the underlying `auth.users` row. Adding a
field here means an admin looking at any user can see it, and the
subject themselves can see it in their `/me` response — but the field
stays off the public [`PublicUserDto`] surface.

active.description:
Account-active flag — a deactivated user couldn't reach `/me`
anyway, but admin needs to see it.

email_verified_at.description:
When the user first demonstrated control of their email. Trust
signal — meaningful to admin (auditing verification status) and
to self (own record), but not to a share picker rendering a
vignette.

federation_issuer.description:
The authority that minted this user's `federation_subject` —
issuer URL for OIDC (id_token `iss` claim), peer domain for OCM,
`None` for local users. Same rationale as `federation_kind`.

federation_kind.description:
Which trust chain minted this user's federation identity —
`"oidc" | "ocm" | "magic_link"` — or `None` for pure local users.
Kept off `PublicUserDto` because a peer's federation kind is a
soft org-affiliation leak; only self + admin need it.

has_password.description:
TRUE when the account has a server-verifiable password
(`password_hash IS NOT NULL`). Kept off `PublicUserDto` because
per-user auth adoption leaks through directory endpoints.

last_login_at.description: Activity signal — private to the subject; admin sees it too.

opaque_migrated.description:
TRUE when the user has completed ≥1 successful OPAQUE login.
Distinct from `opaque_registered`: an admin can invalidate the
envelope leaving the user registered=false but with historical
migrated=true.

opaque_registered.description: TRUE when the user has an OPAQUE envelope on file.

preferred_locale.description:
Subject's own locale preference. Only THEY or an admin managing
them needs this — other callers use their own locale.

storage_quota_bytes.description:
Storage quotas — personal financials. Admin manages others';
self sees own.

user.description: Public identity — same set every authenticated caller sees.

role.description:
Role-keyed since D-Prep cleanup — one row in `storage.role_grants`
is one `GrantDto`. The bundle of underlying permissions is implied
by the role and recomputed client-side from the same lookup table.

can_manage.description:
True when the caller may rename, delete, or change the membership
of this group. v1 computes this as `caller.role == "admin"`. v2
will compute it from per-group `Manage` grants on
`Resource::SubjectGroup(id)` once that resource type lands in
`access_grants`. Frontend reads this unconditionally so the v2
migration is backend-only.

is_virtual.description:
True for system-managed groups (e.g. `Internal`). Membership and
metadata on virtual groups are immutable.

member_count.description:
Direct-member count (users + nested groups, one level only). The
management UI shows this as a chip on each list row; for transitive
expansion size, see the `/effective-members` endpoint.

GroupNameRequest.description: Request body for creating or renaming a group.

HashBatchRequest.description: Request body for the batch hash-ownership check (`POST /api/dedup/check-batch`).

hashes.description: Candidate BLAKE3 hashes (64 hex chars each) to test for ownership.

HashBatchResponse.description: Response for the batch hash-ownership check.

owned.description: The subset of the submitted `hashes` the authenticated user already owns.

existing_size.description: If exists, the size of the existing blob

exists.description: Whether a blob with this hash already exists

hash.description: The BLAKE3 hash that was checked

HeaderPayload.description:
Compact JSON shape written into the header. Fields are documented
in `common::migration_progress::MigrationProgress`.

Public because `GET /api/config` returns the same shape as the
initial hydration snapshot for FE stores — the endpoint mirrors
whatever the header carries so the client has a single wire
vocabulary to render. Frontend treats the value as opaque JSON
and pattern-matches on the fields it currently understands;
adding a field is additive.

oneOf.description:
K3: independent of `readonly` — rotation does NOT engage the
app-wide read-only flag, so the frontend needs a distinct
signal to know "rotation is running, show the rotation
banner instead of migration banner".

unread_count.description:
Unread rows for this user across the whole table — the bell
badge reads this. Kept on the list response so a bell open
doesn't need a second round-trip for the badge.

name.description: Locale name in its own language (e.g., "English", "Español")

dpop_jkt.description:
DPoP JWK thumbprint the client generated at page load. When
present, binds the new session to a browser-held keypair so
stealing the cookie without the private key is useless (RFC
9449). Absent → session is created unbound (fail-open per the
`docs/plan/dpop.md` threat model). Malformed → 400.

username.description:
Identifier the user typed. Accepts BOTH a username (no `@`) and
an email address (`@` present). The server dispatches on
`@`-in-input: with `@` it looks up by email; without, by
username. The two namespaces are provably disjoint (PR 16
forbids `@` in usernames), so a single field handles both
without ambiguity. The frontend submits whatever the user
typed in the "Username or email" field as-is.

marked.description: Number of rows that transitioned unread → read.

from.description: Cluster id being merged into `into`. Deleted after the merge.

into.description:
Cluster id that will absorb the other one (`from`'s photos are
reattributed to `into`; `from` is deleted). Typically the
larger / named cluster wins.

parent_id.description: New parent folder ID (None for root level)

MoveToTrashRequest.description: Request to move an item to trash

NotificationDto.description:
Wire shape for one notification row. `payload` stays a raw JSON
value — per-kind decoding happens on the FE using the `kind`
discriminant.

oneOf.description:
An email actually went out for this recipient. `detail` is
`"magic_link"` (external invitation with a fresh token) or
`"plain_notification"` (internal "you got a new grant" mail).

Skipped silently because this (granter, recipient) pair was
notified less than the coalesce-window ago. The grant is still
recorded; the recipient sees it next time they log in.

Per-recipient hard cap (5/h) reached. The caller may retry after
`retry_after_secs`.

No mail was dispatched for this recipient. `reason` is one of:
- `"recipient_opted_out"`  — user toggled `notify_on_share = false`
- `"operator_disabled"`    — `OXICLOUD_NOTIFY_INTERNAL_USERS_ON_SHARE=false`
- `"no_email"`             — user row has no email on file
- `"oidc_only_no_email"`   — OIDC-only user with no email claim
- `"subject_is_token"`     — anonymous link share (the surface
  that creates the grant or the `/notify` endpoint maps this to 409)

NotifyOutcomeSetDto.description:
The aggregated result of dispatching share notifications for ONE grant
action (one `create_grant` request OR one `/notify` call). Carries
per-recipient outcomes so the frontend can render a single
summary-style toast:

- `total_recipients = 1`, `outcomes[0] = Sent` → "Notified Carol"
- `total_recipients = 1`, `outcomes[0] = Coalesced` → "Carol already
  notified recently"
- `total_recipients = N`, all `Sent` → "Notified all N group members"
- `total_recipients = N`, mix → "Notified 8 of 10 — 2 opted out"

`total_recipients` equals `outcomes.len()` after resolution. For
token-subject grants it is `0` (no human recipient — no toast).

OidcExchangeDto.description: Request body for the OIDC one-time code exchange endpoint

OidcProviderInfoDto.description:
Information about available OIDC providers + self-service auth
methods enabled on the deployment. Consumed by the login page to
decide which forms/buttons to render.

auto_redirect_to_oidc.description:
True iff the effective allowlist is `[Oidc]` AND the
`auto_redirect_if_standalone_oidc` policy is set. Frontend
uses this to decide whether to auto-redirect to the authorize
endpoint on login-page mount (true) or show a click-to-continue
button (false). Default false — the safe posture that avoids
redirect loops when the IdP is degraded.

issuer.description:
The authoritative issuer URL for THIS deployment's OIDC config —
same value that lands on `auth.users.federation_issuer` for
users JIT-provisioned via this IdP.

Populated so the frontend can resolve display: when
`PublicUserDto.federation_issuer` equals this `issuer`, render
`provider_name` as the human-friendly label (avoids showing raw
issuer URLs like `https://sso.example.com/realms/main` in the
admin badge / profile view). Falls back to the raw issuer when
there's no match — happens for legacy rows not yet lazy-rebound,
or (future) users linked to a different IdP than the currently
configured one.

Empty string when OIDC is disabled on this deployment.

magic_link_login_enabled.description:
True iff the server accepts magic-link login requests
(`OXICLOUD_AUTH_METHODS` includes `magic_link` AND SMTP is
configured). Frontend renders the magic-link form when true.

require_verified_email.description:
True iff `OXICLOUD_REQUIRE_VERIFIED_EMAIL` is set. Frontend uses
this hint to explain the `EmailNotVerified` login response and
to nudge new users toward the magic-link verification path
straight after signup.

OpaqueKsfParams.description:
Client-side Argon2id parameters the SPA must feed to
`@serenity-kit/opaque` on `finishRegistration` / `finishLogin`.
Values MUST match the server's `OpaqueConfig::ksf_*` — the
handshake fails to derive matching keys otherwise, so publishing
these is what keeps client and server in lock-step across param
bumps.

OpaqueLoginKe1Dto.description:
Client → server on KE1. `userIdentifier` is the same string the
SPA sends to legacy `/api/auth/login` — email if it contains `@`,
username otherwise (server dispatches on `@`, same as legacy).
`startLoginRequest` is the base64-encoded output of
`ClientLogin::start(...).message`.

OpaqueLoginKe1Response.description:
Server → client on KE1. `exchangeId` is an opaque handle the
client MUST echo back on KE3 (single-use, 60 s TTL); the client
can't derive server state from it. `loginResponse` is the
base64-encoded output of `ServerLogin::start(...).message`.

OpaqueLoginKe3Dto.description:
Client → server on KE3. `exchangeId` matches what KE1 handed
back; `finishLoginRequest` is the base64-encoded output of
`ClientLogin::finish(...).message`.

dpopJkt.description:
DPoP JWK thumbprint the client generated at page load. When
present, binds the new session to a browser-held keypair (RFC
9449). Absent → session created unbound. See `docs/plan/dpop.md`.

OpaqueLookupDto.description:
Client → server on lookup. Same identifier shape as
[`OpaqueLoginKe1Dto::user_identifier`] and legacy
`/api/auth/login`'s `username` field: `@` in the input dispatches
to email lookup, absence → username lookup.

OpaqueLookupResponse.description:
Server → client on lookup. The SPA reads `hasOpaque` to decide
whether to run OPAQUE login (KE1/KE3) or fall back to legacy
`/api/auth/login` (which then silently registers via the Phase 2
hook).

**Anti-enum invariant** — this shape MUST be identical whether
the user exists or not:

  * unknown user           → `hasOpaque: false`
  * user, no envelope      → `hasOpaque: false`
  * user with envelope     → `hasOpaque: true`

A probing attacker cannot distinguish "unknown" from "known but
unregistered" from the response body. The only signal an
attacker gets is "known with envelope" vs "everything else,"
which reveals adoption progress but NOT identity existence.

oneOf.description:
KSF parameters this user's envelope was minted under. Present
only when `has_opaque = true`. The client MUST use these values
(not the ones from `GET /params`) on the login handshake — the
envelope's OPRF derivation was bound to them at register time
and a mismatch will fail the AKE with `InvalidCredentials`.

`None` when: (a) `has_opaque = false` (nothing to publish),
or (b) the envelope predates per-envelope-KSF storage
(migration `20261005000000`) — in which case the client falls
back to `/params` values, which is the same behaviour as
before per-envelope storage existed.

Anti-enum note: the presence of this field ONLY signals what
`has_opaque` already signals (positive existence). Value
differences across users could reveal timing of registration
but not identity — same low-severity leak as the existing
per-identifier probe, no additional exposure.

OpaqueParamsResponse.description:
Payload of `GET /api/auth/opaque/params`. `enabled = false` when
the OPAQUE substrate is not wired for this deployment (mode=off,
or password auth disabled — the same cross-check
`OpaqueConfig::effective_mode` runs). SPA gates the OPAQUE code
path on this flag; when false, it falls back to legacy password
auth as if OPAQUE didn't exist.

`ciphersuiteVersion` + `ksf` are ALWAYS populated (safe defaults
even when `enabled = false`) so a client that ignored `enabled`
wouldn't nil-deref.

OpaqueRegisterFinishDto.description:
Client → server on register KE2. `registrationRecord` is the
base64-encoded output of `ClientRegistration::finish(...).message`;
`ciphersuiteVersion` is what the client believed it was minting
under (compared to the current server value — mismatch → 400).

`ksf*` fields carry the Argon2id parameters the client actually
used at `startRegistration`/`finishRegistration` time. Server
persists them per-envelope so future changes to the server's
`OpaqueConfig::ksf_*` don't invalidate this envelope. Optional
on the wire (older clients that predate per-envelope storage
omit them; server falls back to its current config in that case).

OpaqueRegisterStartDto.description:
Client → server on register KE1. `registrationRequest` is the
base64-encoded output of the client's
`ClientRegistration::start(...).message`.

OpaqueRegisterStartResponse.description:
Server → client on register KE1. `registrationResponse` is the
base64-encoded output of `ServerRegistration::start(...).message`.
Also echoes `ciphersuiteVersion` so the client can reject a
mid-flight suite change and abort before uploading.

OutgoingResourceGrantDto.description: One (subject, permissions) entry within an outgoing resource item.

has_password.description: Whether the token has a password set. Always `false` for user subjects.

is_external.description:
True when the subject is a magic-link-only external user
(PR N2). Always `false` for token and group subjects, and for
internal users. Used by the My Shares per-row menu to choose
between "Resend invitation email" (external) and "Notify by
email" (internal).

role.description:
Role label: `"viewer"` | `"commenter"` | `"contributor"` | `"editor"`
| `"owner"`. Emitted by `role_from_permissions()` during the dual-write
window; once D-Prep cleanup lands this is read directly from
`storage.role_grants.role`. The legacy `"admin"` spelling is no longer
emitted — clients that cached it must accept `"owner"` too (the API
`Role::parse` still accepts `"admin"` on input for one release).

subject_display.description: Human-readable label (username for users, share name for tokens).

OutgoingResourceItemDto.description: One item in the my-shares list.

first_shared_at.description: Earliest grant date across all subjects on this resource.

resource.description: Full resource details. Shape is determined by `resource_type`.

PaginationDto.description: A DTO to represent pagination information

has_next.description: Indicates if there is a next page

has_prev.description: Indicates if there is a previous page

PaginationRequestDto.description: A DTO to represent a pagination request

PersonDto.description: A named (or unnamed) identity cluster, with a cover photo for its tile.

cover_file_id.description: File id of the cover face's photo, for the tile thumbnail.

name.description: `None` until the user names the person.

ProgressHeader.description:
Shared progress shape used by both `migration` and `rotation`
header fields — same struct name, same JSON field names. Frontend
treats them identically at the render layer.

PublicUserDto.description:
Public identity — what any authenticated caller may see about ANOTHER
user. Returned by `/api/users/{id}` and everywhere a user is
referenced by another surface (share responses, group members,
magic-link invitees, recipient enrichment).

This is the audience-narrowest DTO: adding a field here means every
authenticated caller can see it about every visible user. Fields that
are meaningful only to the subject themselves (preferences, session
state) or only to an admin (auth adoption signals) belong on
[`SelfUserDto`] or [`FullUserDto`] respectively.

image.description:
Avatar payload (base64 data-URI up to 512 KiB). Public so a share
picker can render the recipient's face directly. Will move to a
dedicated avatar endpoint in a future refactor — this shape is
transitional.

is_external.description:
`true` for grant-only external recipients (magic-link, OIDC-only,
future OCM federated). Renders the "external" badge on the vignette.

is_online.description:
Presence signal — TRUE when the server observed a request on any
of this user's non-revoked sessions within the last
[`ONLINE_WINDOW`](crate::application::dtos::session_dto::ONLINE_WINDOW)
(5 min). Sourced from an EXISTS subquery when the DTO is built
from a list-projection path; single-user endpoints that don't
enrich presence ship `false`.

role.description:
Role string ("admin" | "user"). Kept public because the sharee /
group-member vignette renders an admin badge.

RecentItemDto.description:
DTO for recent items, enriched with item metadata via SQL JOIN
so the frontend does not need N+1 requests to resolve names/sizes.

icon_class.description: FontAwesome icon CSS class (e.g. "fas fa-file-image", "fas fa-folder")

icon_special_class.description: Extra CSS class for icon styling (e.g. "image-icon", "folder-icon")

id.description: Unique identifier for the recent item

item_name.description: Display name of the file or folder

item_path.description:
Full human-readable path (e.g. "Documents/Work" for a folder,
"Documents/Work/report.pdf" for a file)

item_size.description: Size in bytes (files only; folders → None)

parent_id.description: Parent folder ID (folder_id for files, parent_id for folders)

size_formatted.description: Formatted file size (e.g. "3.27 MB"); "--" for folders

accessed_at.description: When the resource was last accessed.

resource.description: Full resource details — shape determined by `resource_type`.

password.description:
Optional password (≥8 chars when present). When omitted, a
welcome magic-link is mailed to `email` for first-session
bootstrap. The user can later set a password via the
change-password endpoint to switch to classic username/email +
password login.

username.description:
Optional handle (2-64 chars, no `@`). When omitted, the user can
claim one later via the profile-edit endpoint. Users without a
username cannot use NextCloud clients or create app passwords
(Basic-Auth resolves users by username); web UI / native API
works fine without one.

name.description:
New display name for the cluster. `null` or omitted clears
the name, reverting the cluster to its "Unnamed" state.

ResourceContentDto.description:
The resource payload for one item in the shared-with-me list.

The variant is discriminated by `resource_type` on the parent
[`SharedWithMeItemDto`].  Serialised as the inner object (no wrapper key)
via `#[serde(untagged)]`, so consumers see the file/folder fields directly
under the `resource` key.

RestoreFromTrashRequest.description: Request to restore an item from trash

RoleDto.description:
Wire-format wrapper around the domain `Role` enum. Carries the
serde/utoipa derives. Maps 1:1 to/from `Role` via `From`.

The historical `"admin"` alias for `Owner` (used during the D-Prep
dual-write window for cached clients) has been retired in the cleanup
PR — the OxiCloud UI emits `"owner"` exclusively. Stragglers receive
a 422 on POST/PUT, which surfaces the upgrade cleanly.

SaveOidcSettingsDto.description: Request body for saving OIDC settings from the admin panel

client_secret.description: Only update if provided and non-empty (None = keep existing)

SaveStorageSettingsDto.description: Request body for saving storage settings from the admin panel

s3_access_key.description: Only update if provided and non-empty (None = keep existing)

s3_secret_key.description: Only update if provided and non-empty (None = keep existing)

SearchCriteriaDto.description:
* Data Transfer Object for file search criteria.
 *
 * This structure represents all possible search parameters that can be used
 * to filter files and folders in the system. It supports various filter types
 * including name matching, file types, date ranges, and size constraints.

created_after.description: Optional minimum creation date (seconds since epoch)

created_before.description: Optional maximum creation date (seconds since epoch)

file_types.description: Optional list of file extensions to include (e.g., "pdf", "jpg")

folder_id.description: Optional folder ID to limit search scope

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return

max_size.description: Optional maximum file size in bytes

min_size.description: Optional minimum file size in bytes

modified_after.description: Optional minimum modification date (seconds since epoch)

modified_before.description: Optional maximum modification date (seconds since epoch)

name_contains.description: Optional text to search in file/folder names

recursive.description: Whether to search recursively within subfolders (default: true)

reverse.description:
Reverse the sort direction — descending for name/size/date,
no-op for `relevance` (a descending relevance sort is meaningless).

sort_by.description:
Sort dimension. Canonical set: `"relevance"` | `"name"` | `"size"`
| `"updated_at"` | `"created_at"`. Direction is `reverse` below —
the `_desc` suffix pattern was retired 2026-07-26 in favour of
a single boolean, so every consumer treats "which column" and
"which direction" as orthogonal concerns.

SearchFileResultDto.description:
A file search result enriched with server-computed metadata.

Phase 1-plus extension (AuthZ-adjacent audit follow-up, 2026-07-26):
carries `etag`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `is_favorite`, `is_shared`
through from `FileDto`. Pre-fix these fields were dropped at `enrich_file`
time, so the wire-normalised `SearchResourcesDto` handler couldn't
reconstruct a full `FileDto` for its `resource` slot — every result
looked unfavorited / unshared, and provenance was blank. The extra
columns come from `file_blob_read_repository.rs::search_files_paginated`
(SELECT'd inline, EXISTS subqueries for the caller-scoped booleans).

blob_hash.description:
Raw BLAKE3 content hash. Feeds `FileDto::content_hash` and
`File::compute_etag` when search results are converted to
`FileDto` (NC REPORT/SEARCH response). Defaults to `String::new()`
for backward-compatible deserialisation of cached results
that pre-date the column.

created_by.description:
§14 provenance — user that originally created this file. `None`
when the referenced user has been deleted or for legacy rows.

etag.description:
HTTP ETag — derived from `blob_hash + modified_at`. Duplicates
`FileDto::etag` so the wire handler can hand a client the same
token for `If-Match` / `If-None-Match` conditional requests on
search results as it would on a folder listing.

icon_class.description: CSS icon class for the file type (e.g., "fas fa-file-pdf")

icon_special_class.description: Extra CSS class for icon styling (e.g., "pdf-icon", "code-icon js-icon")

is_favorite.description:
Caller-scoped: `true` when the requesting user has favorited
this file. Populated by an EXISTS subquery in the search SQL —
the search repo carries it back as a per-row bool that the
service plumbs into this DTO.

is_shared.description:
Resource-scoped: `true` when the file has ANY explicit role-grant.
Populated by the sibling EXISTS on `storage.role_grants`.

match_source.description:
Where the match came from: "name" (filename matched the query) or
"content" (discovered via the full-text content index).

mime_type.description:
MIME type — `Arc<str>` so enrichment reuses `FileDto`'s interned
value (an atomic increment) instead of allocating per result row.

snippet.description:
Plain-text fragment around the first content match, present only for
hits discovered through the full-text content index.

updated_by.description: §14 provenance — user that performed the most recent mutation.

SearchFolderResultDto.description:
A folder search result enriched with server-computed metadata.

See `SearchFileResultDto` for the Phase 1-plus rationale — same
story: the six caller/provenance fields are carried through so the
wire-normalised handler can hand the frontend a complete `FolderDto`.

created_by.description: §14 provenance — creator user id. `None` for legacy folders.

drive_id.description:
Drive that owns this folder. Same column as `storage.folders.drive_id`,
carried through so downstream callers (e.g. the NC search REPORT
handler) can populate `FolderDto::drive_id` without a fallback sentinel.

etag.description:
HTTP ETag — folders derive theirs from the tree-etag propagator.
Duplicating it here keeps the wire handler's `FolderDto`
reconstruction complete.

is_favorite.description:
Caller-scoped: `true` when the requesting user has favorited
this folder. EXISTS on `auth.user_favorites`.

is_root.description: Whether it is a root folder

is_shared.description:
Resource-scoped: `true` when the folder has any explicit
role-grant. EXISTS on `storage.role_grants`.

SearchMeta.description:
Search-specific per-item metadata (relevance score, snippet, hit
source). Sits inline on each `SearchResourceItem` so consumers get
data locality — no keyed lookup. `ResourceList` ignores the field.

Wire keys are shortened (`meta.score`, `meta.via`) vs the internal
`SearchFileResultDto` field names (`relevance_score`, `match_source`)
to keep the envelope compact on large result pages.

snippet.description:
Plain-text fragment around the first content-index hit. Absent
for name-only matches and for folder results.

via.description:
Where the hit came from: `"name"` or `"content"`. Absent when the
origin is ambiguous (empty query → everything matches).

SearchResourceItem.description:
One search result — same `resource_type + resource` shape as the
`/*/resources` envelopes so `ResourceList` consumes it as-is, plus
the inline `meta` for search-specific enrichment.

resource.description:
Full resource details (untagged: `FileDto | FolderDto | DriveDto`).
Shape determined by `resource_type`.

SearchResourcesDto.description:
Response envelope for `GET /api/search` — cursor-paginated + search
metadata. `total` is an approximate caller-visible count (permission-
filtered) when the service can compute it cheaply, absent otherwise —
matches sibling envelope endpoints, which all serialise counts as
integers (see `app_password_dto`, `plugin_dto`, `pagination`).

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent on the last page.

query_time_ms.description:
Server-side query time. UI shows "Found N in Xms" and admins use
it as a health signal.

total.description:
Approximate caller-visible total match count. Never leaks a count
for rows the caller cannot see. Omitted when unknown.

SearchResultsDto.description:
* Data Transfer Object for search results.
 *
 * This structure encapsulates the results of a search operation, including
 * both files and folders that match the search criteria, along with pagination
 * information and server-computed metadata.

files.description: Files matching the search criteria (enriched with metadata)

folders.description: Folders matching the search criteria (enriched with metadata)

has_more.description: Whether there are more results available

total_count.description: Total count of matching items (for pagination)

icon_special_class.description: Extra CSS class for icon styling

SearchSuggestionsDto.description: DTO for search suggestion results (quick prefix search)

suggestions.description: Suggested file/folder names matching the query prefix

SelfUserDto.description:
Self view — everything the caller may see about themselves.
Returned by `/api/auth/me` and by every `AuthResponseDto` path
(login / refresh / OIDC callback / magic-link redemption).

Composed on top of [`FullUserDto`] so `/me` and `/admin/users` share
the SAME "full profile" contract for the fields both need — new
self+admin-visible fields go on `FullUserDto` and both endpoints get
them together. Fields here are pure self-scoped state: preferences,
session-scoped flags, and caller-scoped permissions.

can_edit_image.description:
Caller-scoped permission: can I edit my own avatar? `false` for
OIDC users whose avatar comes from the IdP. Only meaningful when
caller == subject; nonsense on any other DTO.

force_password_change.description:
Admin-set temp-password gate — SPA nav guard blocks everything
but `/change-password` until this flips back. Cleared by a
successful `POST /api/auth/change-password`.

full.description: Full profile — same shape as one row of `/api/admin/users`.

is_dpop_bound.description:
Session-scoped: my current session carries a DPoP thumbprint.
SPA reads this on `session.load()` to skip a redundant
`POST /api/auth/dpop/bind` when the session is already bound.

ui_preferences.description:
Opaque UI preferences bag — my own UI state. Cross-device store
for pure UI toggles (view mode, sidebar collapse, hide dotfiles,
…). The server never inspects the contents. Always present on
the wire; empty bag is `{}`, never `null`.

SendSmtpTestDto.description:
Request body for `POST /api/admin/smtp/test`: send a hardcoded
diagnostic email to the given recipient.

ServerConfigDto.description:
Server-configuration DTO. Additive over time — clients ignore
unknown fields, and no field is ever repurposed (same discipline
as JSON-RPC error codes on the message bus).

auth.description:
Auth-related tunables the SPA needs to gate submit locally.
Composes with `/api/auth/oidc/providers` — that endpoint lists
federation options; this one carries the numeric thresholds
(password length today, more later) that the form has to check
before firing the request.

features.description:
Feature flags — which subsystems the server has enabled.
Clients gate optional UI on these (e.g. hide the notification
bell if `features.message_bus` is false, since the bell would
have no delivery channel).

server_status.description:
Live server-status snapshot — exact same shape and field
names as the `X-Server-Status` response header. Clients use
this to hydrate their reactive store at boot; subsequent live
changes propagate through the header on every other request
(the middleware and this endpoint share `build_header_payload`
so drift is impossible). Non-optional so the client always
has a definite value; `readonly: false` with no `migration`
or `rotation` is the "everything nominal" case.

version.description:
Server version — `OXICLOUD_VERSION` derived by `build.rs` from
the git tag / `GITHUB_REF_NAME` / `git describe`. Matches what
`GET /api/version` returns. Cargo.toml stays pinned at `0.0.0`;
this string is the canonical build identity.

SessionOrigin.description:
How a session was originally minted. Set at INSERT by the login
handler; carried over on refresh (a rotation doesn't change how the
user first authenticated). Stored as `text` server-side with a CHECK
constraint — see `migrations/20261013000000_sessions_origin.sql`.

`serde(rename_all = "snake_case")` so the wire values match the
column values one-to-one: `password | opaque | magic_link | oidc |
unknown`. `Unknown` is the fallback for pre-migration rows and any
future login path that hasn't been taught to stamp an origin yet.

SessionSummaryDto.description:
Wire shape for `GET /api/admin/sessions`. Contains everything the
admin table renders and **nothing the raw session entity would
leak** (refresh token, OIDC ID-token, full DPoP thumbprint).

dpop_jkt_prefix.description:
First 8 chars of the DPoP thumbprint when bound, `None` otherwise.
Enough to distinguish two bindings of the same user across
devices at a glance; not enough to leak the full jkt.

is_active.description:
Whether this row is currently usable — `!revoked && expires_at > now()`.
Kept server-side so the SPA doesn't drift if the browser clock is off.
**Distinct from [`is_online`](Self::is_online)** — this is a
*lifecycle* signal (row still has authority), that one is a
*presence* signal (a request landed on it lately).

is_bound.description:
`true` iff the session is DPoP-bound. Rendered as a lock icon
in the admin table. Complements the auth-badges surface.

is_current.description:
`true` when this row IS the caller's currently-active session —
set by the service layer by comparing the row's `dpop_jkt` with
the caller's own bound thumbprint. Lets the admin panel flag
"revoking this cuts your own branch" so an admin doesn't
accidentally log themselves out. `false` when either side is
unbound (can't correlate) or when the jkts don't match.

is_online.description:
Whether the session was actually observed serving a request in the
last [`ONLINE_WINDOW`] (5 min). Presence signal, orthogonal to
[`is_active`](Self::is_active): a session may be active-and-online
(green dot in the admin table), active-and-idle (no dot, "last
seen 12 min ago"), or non-active-and-offline (expired / revoked
rows are never online). Derived server-side against
[`ONLINE_WINDOW`] so the row-level badge stays consistent with
the `oxicloud_sessions_online[_users]` Prometheus aggregates.

Guaranteed `false` for revoked / expired rows — those short-
circuit before the recency check so a revoked row that happened
to receive a request in its final second before revocation
doesn't confusingly render "Online" post-revocation.

is_revoked.description:
`true` when the row is revoked. Present because the panel has an
opt-in "include revoked" checkbox — active-only listings will
always show `false` here, but forensics listings need the flag.

last_seen_at.description:
Wall-clock time this session was last observed serving an
authenticated request. Moved forward per request by the
in-process [`LastSeenTracker`](crate::infrastructure::services::last_seen_tracker)
via a batched UPDATE every 30 s — so this value trails the
true "last seen" by at most one flush interval on a running
server. On DB read it always converges after a graceful
shutdown flush. Distinct from `created_at`: that only moves
on session rotation (silent refresh), so its resolution is
capped at the access-token TTL. The admin table renders a
"last seen X ago" column off this field.

origin.description:
How the session was minted — see [`SessionOrigin`]. Set at
INSERT time by the login handler and carried over on refresh
(rotation doesn't change how the user first authenticated).
Drives the admin panel's origin column + filter.

SetupAdminDto.description:
DTO for the one-time initial admin setup endpoint (`/api/setup`).
Available only when the system is not yet initialized (no admin exists).

SharedWithMeItemDto.description:
One item in the shared-with-me list.

`resource_type` indicates whether `resource` contains a file or a folder.
Using a single `resource` field (instead of nullable `file`/`folder` pairs)
makes adding new resource types backward-compatible — only `resource_type`
gains a new variant; the wrapper shape stays the same.

granted_at.description: Earliest grant date for this resource.

granted_by.description: UUID of the user who created the (earliest) grant.

permissions.description: All permissions the caller holds on this resource (aggregated).

resource.description: Full resource details. Shape is determined by `resource_type`.

SharegrantedPayload.description:
Payload written on the DB row when a `share_granted` notification
is created. Kind = [`kind::SHARE_GRANTED`].

The `resource_name` and `resource_path` fields are snapshotted at
grant time — even if the resource is later renamed or moved, the
notification still reflects what it was called when the share
happened. `resource_path` is populated for kinds addressable via
`/files/[...path]` (folders + files); `None` for calendars,
address books, playlists, drives.

Wire form matches the `payload` JSONB column exactly — Rust is
the source of truth, OpenAPI schema auto-derives via
`#[derive(ToSchema)]`. Adding a new field is additive on the
JSONB column; no migration needed.

expires_at.description: Grant expiry, if bounded. `None` = never expires.

granter_id.description: The user who created the grant.

navigate_folder_id.description:
FE-navigation hint — the folder id the notification link
should route to. Populated when `resource_type` isn't itself
a folder-shaped resource but the FE still wants to land in
`/files/{id}` (concretely: **drives** — the recipient lands
on the drive's root folder). For `resource_type == 'folder'`
the FE uses `resource_id` directly and this field stays
`None`; same for `file` (routes to `/shared-with-me?file=`
via a different path). `None` for calendar / address_book /
playlist — those aren't reachable via `/files/*` at all.

resource_name.description:
Display name at grant time. `None` if the lookup failed at
ingest (bell renders a generic fallback in that case).

resource_path.description:
Storage path at grant time. Populated for
`folder` / `file` kinds; `None` for other kinds.

resource_type.description:
Resource kind slug: `folder`, `file`, `drive`, `calendar`,
`address_book`, `playlist`. Same string form as
[`crate::domain::services::authorization::Resource::type_str`].

role.description:
Role granted (`viewer`, `editor`, `owner`, …). Same string
form as [`crate::domain::services::authorization::Role::as_str`].

SmtpInfoDto.description:
Read-only SMTP info shown on the admin SMTP page. SMTP configuration
is sourced exclusively from environment variables — these fields are
for display only and any change has to happen by updating the env
and restarting the server.

enabled.description: Whether `OXICLOUD_SMTP_HOST` is set and SMTP construction succeeded.

user_state.description:
`<set>` if a SASL user is configured, `<anon>` otherwise.
Never echoes the username — admins compare against the
runtime config without having to look in `.env`.

SmtpTestResultDto.description:
Result of a `POST /api/admin/smtp/test` invocation. `success=true`
carries the SMTP server's response code + first reply line; on
failure the relevant error message goes in `error`. Always 200 OK
so the frontend can render both outcomes in one place — the SMTP
failure is a normal operational state, not an HTTP error.

code.description: SMTP status code (e.g. 250). Only set on success.

error.description: Human-readable error message. Only set on failure.

message.description: First line of the SMTP server's reply. Only set on success.

StartMigrationDto.description:
Request body for `POST /api/admin/storage/migration/start`.

**Multi-entry contract** (see `docs/plan/storage-multi-entry.md`):
`target_name` is REQUIRED — it names the storage entry the copy
job will move blobs INTO. The admin picks it from the entries
declared in `OXICLOUD_STORAGE_ENTRIES`. The trigger endpoint
rejects the request when the name doesn't exist or equals the
currently-active entry (no-op guard).

concurrency.description:
How many blobs to copy in parallel (default: 4).

**Currently ignored** — the recoverable copy loop is
sequential (one blob at a time within the batch). Kept in
the DTO for wire-compat with the admin UI form; will be
honoured once per-batch fan-out lands (dual-write /
concurrent-copy future slice).

target_name.description:
Name of the storage entry to migrate blobs INTO. Must be
present in `OXICLOUD_STORAGE_ENTRIES` and must differ from
the currently-active entry.

total_logical_bytes.description: Total logical bytes (what users think they have)

total_references.description: Total number of references (files pointing to blobs)

unique_blobs.description: Total number of unique blobs stored

oneOf.description:
Invite-by-email. Lazily provisions an external user with the
normalised address as both username and email when no match
exists; otherwise reuses the existing user. Triggers a magic-link
invitation email when the resolved user has no other login
credential.

SubjectInputDto.description:
Subject shape accepted by `POST /api/grants`. Internally-tagged enum
so the existing `{type:"user", id:"..."}` payload keeps working
alongside the new `{type:"email", email:"..."}` variant that feeds
the invite-by-email flow. The response-side [`SubjectDto`] stays
unchanged — externals resolve to `Subject::User(uuid)` with
`is_external = TRUE` on the user row, never a distinct subject type.

admin_count.description: Number of admin users in the system.

initialized.description: Whether the system has been set up with an admin.

TransferOwnershipDto.description:
Request body for transferring server ownership.

Separate from [`UpdateUserRoleDto`] on purpose: ownership is not an
assignable role. The generic role endpoint refuses `"owner"`, because
conferring it there would create a second owner rather than move the
one that exists.

new_owner_id.description:
The user who becomes the new owner. The caller — who must be the
current owner — is demoted to admin in the same transaction.

key.description: The translation key that was not found

locale.description: The locale code used for translation
The locale code used for translation

TrashResourceItemDto.description:
One item in a `GET /api/trash/resources` page.

`deletion_date` is the real timestamp at which the item will be permanently
deleted (= `trashed_at + retention_days`). The client derives "days until
deletion" itself from this + the current clock — the wire format does not
duplicate that derivation. `resource.path` carries the original location
(soft-delete preserves the row's `path` column).

deletion_date.description: When the item will be permanently deleted by the retention sweeper.

drive_id.description:
The drive the trashed item belongs to. Enables client-side
group-by-drive in the `/trash` UI (D2b spec — see
`project_trash_groupbys_d2b` memory). The drive's display name
resolves through the `/api/drives` listing the client already
holds in `drives.svelte` — no extra round-trip needed.

resource.description: Full resource details — shape determined by `resource_type`.

trashed_at.description: When the user moved the item to trash.

TrashedItemDto.description: DTO representing an item in the trash

icon_class.description: FontAwesome icon class for the file type

icon_special_class.description: Special CSS class for icon styling (e.g., "image-icon", "pdf-icon")

UpdateAddressBookRequest.description: Request body for updating an address book.

UpdateContactRequest.description: Request body for updating a contact (all fields optional).

expires_at.description: Optional. Pass `null` (or omit) to clear an existing expiry.

UpdateDrivePoliciesDto.description:
Body for `PATCH /api/drives/{id}/policies` (D5).

Partial merge: any field left out of the JSON keeps its current
JSONB value (the repo uses `policies || $partial`). Each field
defaults to `false` in `DrivePolicies`, but the merge is keyed on
presence — so omitting a field means "leave it alone", not "set
it to false". Clients flip a single key at a time without
round-tripping the whole bag.

UpdateDriveQuotaDto.description:
Body for `PATCH /api/drives/{id}/quota` (D4).

`quota_bytes = null` (or ≤ 0) means unlimited — matches the DB
convention where NULL on the row is treated as "no cap" by
`storage_usage_service::check_drive_quota`. The service
normalises 0/negative to None before writing.

quota_bytes.description:
New quota in bytes. `null` (or omitted) or ≤ 0 → unlimited.
A value below the drive's current `used_bytes` is accepted
intentionally (soft-quota semantic — new writes gated,
existing content untouched; owners recover by deleting
until the drive comes back under the cap).

description.description: Reserved for future use; v1 only persists the name in `rename`.

UpdateProfileDto.description:
Partial-update body for `PATCH /api/auth/me/profile` (PR 24).

Each field is **optional**:
- **absent** → no change to that field.
- **present** → set / claim.

**Username is claim-once, immutable.** This endpoint accepts
`username` only when the caller currently has none — passing it
when one is already claimed is rejected with `409 UsernameImmutable`.
The immutability avoids the NextCloud / DAV client breakage that
would otherwise come from renaming (paths under
`/remote.php/dav/files/{user}/…` and the `verify_url_user` check
both bake the username in as a stable identifier). If a user really
typoed their handle and needs to fix it, an admin override is the
escape hatch.

**Given / family name** are freely settable. Any non-empty value
replaces the current one. Clearing back to `None` is out of scope
for v1.

**OIDC-linked users are rejected wholesale with 403** — their
profile fields are managed at the IdP. The IdP is the source of
truth; mirroring writes here would just create a divergence.

family_name.description: New last/family name. Same semantics as `given_name`.

given_name.description:
New first/given name. Any non-empty value sets/replaces the
current value. Absent → no change.

notify_on_share.description:
Whether to receive an email when someone shares a resource with
the user. Absent → no change (existing setting preserved). Pass
`true` to opt in, `false` to opt out. Honored only on the
plain-notification path; magic-link first-invitations to externals
always send.

preferred_locale.description:
New preferred locale (BCP-47 shape, e.g. `"fr"`, `"zh-TW"`).
Must resolve against the server's `LocaleRegistry` — unknown
codes are rejected with 400. Pass an empty string to clear the
preference back to the server default (the application layer
normalises `""` → `None`).

ui_preferences.description:
Partial patch into the opaque UI preferences bag. **Must be a
JSON object.** Applied via a SHALLOW merge on the server:
keys present here overwrite existing top-level keys; keys not
present survive. A key value of `null` REMOVES that key from
the bag (implemented via `jsonb_strip_nulls` after the merge).

Example: current bag `{"a":1,"b":2}`, patch `{"b":3,"c":4}`
→ merged `{"a":1,"b":3,"c":4}`. Patch `{"a":null}` → `{"b":2}`.

Absent → no change to the bag. This is a UI-only surface;
server never inspects the keys.

username.description:
Handle to claim (2-64 chars, `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`, no `@`).
Accepted only when the caller currently has no username. Once
claimed the handle is permanent for the lifetime of the
account; subsequent attempts to set or change it via this
endpoint are rejected with 409. Admin override (via the
admin-create-user / admin-update-user surface, future PR) is
the escape hatch for genuine typos.

UpdateRoleDto.description: `PUT /api/grants/role` — reconcile a subject's role on a resource.

expires_at.description: Optional expiry applied to every grant written or updated by this call.

UpdateUserActiveDto.description: Request body for updating a user's active status

UpdateUserQuotaDto.description: Request body for updating a user's storage quota

quota_bytes.description: Quota in bytes. Use 0 for unlimited.

UpdateUserRoleDto.description: Request body for updating a user's role

UpgradeToInternalDto.description:
Body for `POST /api/auth/upgrade-to-internal`. Converts an
authenticated external user into an internal user with their own
personal drive.

`password` is optional — semantics decided per deployment:
  * If `magic_link` is in `OXICLOUD_AUTH_METHODS` (and OIDC isn't
    enabled) → password can be omitted; user remains magic-link-only
    for login after upgrade.
  * Otherwise → password is required; refusal returns 400
    `error_type = "PasswordRequired"`. Without it the upgraded user
    would have no login path.

UploadStatusResponseDto.description: Response for querying upload session status.
